intro: To get info on a file in Finder on Mac, click the file to select it, then choose File > Get Info or press Command-I. The information window shows the file's type, size, dates and location, plus sharing and permissions when they apply.
tldr: Click the file once, then press Command-I or choose File > Get Info.
The window shows the type, size, dates and where the file is stored.
For several files, hold Control and choose File > Get Summary Info, which opens one window per file.
Disk permissions sit under Sharing & Permissions. Click the lock if it is closed.
Ask Lazur where Get Info is and it points at the menu item. You still make the click.

blocks.text: Get Info is the Finder window that describes a single file, a folder or a disk. It shows what kind of item you have, how big it is and when it last changed. You can open it with a keyboard shortcut or from the menu bar. Apple's Mac User Guide is the source for these steps, and it shows macOS 27 in its version menu. Older macOS versions were not checked, so menu names there may differ slightly.
Fastest way: select the file and press Command-I

Most of the time you need a quick answer. You want to know how big a file is, or when you last changed it. Click the file once in a Finder window or on the desktop. Then press Command-I. The information window opens. If you prefer the mouse, go to File > Get Info in the menu bar at the top of the screen. Both routes open the same window. The shortcut is faster once it becomes a habit. The menu is the safer choice when you do not remember the keys.

blocks.text: What the Get Info window shows

The window lists facts about the item. For a typical file you see its type, its size and when it was last modified. You also see where it is stored. Apple's iCloud guide lists the same kind of fields for iCloud Drive files: type, size, last modified date, storage location, and who shared the item if it is shared. Finder's window is the one to use for files on your Mac.

Read the size first. It is the number people look for most often. If you want to know how much room a folder takes up, select the folder and open its Get Info window. Then compare that figure with the free space on the disk. Treat the number as a guide when you plan a cleanup, not as an exact accounting.

Some sections collapse. Click the small disclosure arrow next to a section name to open or close it. Apple's permissions guide uses this arrow for Sharing & Permissions, and the same pattern applies to other sections. The sections you see depend on the item, so do not expect every window to match.
Get info on several files at once

Get Info works on one item at a time by default. To see details for a group, select the files first. Hold the Control key, then open the File menu and choose Get Summary Info. Apple says a separate information window opens for each item. A big selection creates a big pile of windows, so start with a small batch. Close them as you go, or you will lose track of which window belongs to which file.
Check sharing and permissions for a disk

Permissions decide who can read, change or copy an item. Apple's permissions guide starts with a disk, so begin there. Select the disk in Finder, then choose File > Get Info. Expand Sharing & Permissions with its disclosure arrow. If the lock in the bottom-right corner is closed, click it so the settings open. The guide does not show the exact prompt you will see, so follow what macOS asks.

One checkbox needs a note. Apple's guide mentions Ignore ownership on this volume. That checkbox is for disks, and it does not appear for disks used for Time Machine backups. If you are not an administrator, Apple's guide says to ask an administrator for access. Changing ownership on a shared drive can lock other people out, so check with them first.
Get file details for iCloud Drive on iCloud.com

You do not need a Mac to check an iCloud Drive file. Open icloud.com/iclouddrive in a browser and sign in. Select the file or folder, click the More button in the top-right corner, and choose Get Info. The panel shows the file type, size, last modified date, where it is stored and who shared it. It shows fewer fields than Finder, and it covers iCloud Drive only.

Size matters more when storage is tight. Apple's storage page says each account gets 5 GB of free storage. The same page lists US iCloud+ prices, including $0.99 a month for 50 GB and $9.99 a month for 2 TB. The page is dated September 16, 2026, and prices vary by country. Use Get Info to find the large files before you decide what to delete or move.
Quicker ways to see more while you browse

Two view settings put details on screen without opening a window. Open View > Show Path Bar to display the folder path inside the Finder window. Hold Option to see it briefly if it is hidden. Control-click a folder in the path bar and choose Copy "folder" as Pathname to copy its path. You can then paste that path into a document or a message.

Item info is the other option. Choose View > Show View Options and select Show item info. Apple says this option appears only in Icon view, so switch to Icon view first. The details then sit under each icon. That helps when you want to scan a folder without opening every file.
Mistakes people make with Get Info

items: Pressing Command-I while another app is active. The shortcut acts on the front app, so click the Finder window or the desktop first.
Clicking empty space instead of the file. Get Info needs the file highlighted, so click its name or icon.
Expecting the Ignore ownership checkbox on a Time Machine disk. It does not appear there.
Trying to edit permissions without clicking the lock. The settings stay closed until you click it.
Assuming iCloud.com shows everything Finder shows. The web panel has fewer fields.
Opening many Get Info windows at once. Each file gets its own window, so close them when you finish.

blocks.text: Fixing Video Duration problems on Tahoe

blocks.title: Video Duration shows --:--
blocks.text: One Apple Community thread from a macOS 26.0 (Tahoe) user reports that video files show --:-- for Duration in Get Info. The thread has no Apple or moderator confirmation of a cause or fix.

The workaround in that thread uses QuickTime Player. Open the video in QuickTime Player, press Command-I, and read the Inspector. You get the metadata without relying on the Finder window. The sources checked for this page do not say whether Apple removed the field on purpose or fixed it in a later update.
Where Get Info fits in your next steps

Get Info answers one question at a time. Once you know a file's details, the next step is often organizing it. [Add a tag to a file in Finder](/how-to/add-a-tag-to-a-file-in-finder) helps you group work by project. [Search for a file in Finder](/how-to/search-for-a-file-in-finder) helps when you cannot find the item. [Show hidden files in Finder](/how-to/show-hidden-files-in-finder) helps when a file you expect is missing from the list. You can also [change the sidebar in Finder](/how-to/change-the-sidebar-in-finder) to keep your most-used folders in reach.
How Lazur helps with Get Info

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold Option and Command, then ask about anything on your screen. Ask where Get Info is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask Lazur to walk you through it, and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. Lazur does not click buttons or operate Finder for you. Your hand makes every click.

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to get an answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

Check the file before you change it

Get Info is a safe place to look. Opening the window does not change the file. Changes happen only when you edit a field or a permission setting. That makes it a good first step before you clean up a folder. Read the size, check the modified date, and then decide what to do.

faq.question: What is the keyboard shortcut for Get Info in Finder on Mac?
faq.answer: Select the file in Finder, then press Command-I. Apple's Get Info guide lists this shortcut. If it does not respond, click the file again, check that Finder is the active app, or choose File > Get Info from the menu bar.

faq.question: How do I get info on several files at once in Finder?
faq.answer: Select the files, hold the Control key, then open the File menu and choose Get Summary Info. Apple says a separate information window opens for each item, so select a small group at a time.

faq.question: Why do some Get Info windows show fewer sections?
faq.answer: The sections depend on the item. Apple's iCloud guide lists type, size, last modified date, storage location and sharing for iCloud Drive files. Expand any section with its disclosure arrow. Section names on other macOS versions may differ from these steps.

faq.question: How do I check file permissions with Get Info?
faq.answer: Apple's permissions guide starts with a disk. Select the disk, choose File > Get Info, expand Sharing & Permissions, and click the lock if it is closed. If you are not an administrator, ask an administrator for access.

faq.question: Can I get info on an iCloud Drive file without a Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Open icloud.com/iclouddrive, select the file or folder, click More in the top-right corner, and choose Get Info. The panel shows fewer fields than Finder and covers iCloud Drive files only.

faq.question: Why does Duration show --:-- for my video on Tahoe?
faq.answer: One Apple Community thread from a macOS 26.0 user reports this. The thread has no Apple confirmation of a cause or fix. The workaround is to open the video in QuickTime Player and press Command-I to use the Inspector.

faq.question: Does Lazur open Get Info for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate Finder. Ask where Get Info is and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask for a walkthrough and it guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

faq.question: Does opening Get Info change my file?
faq.answer: Opening the window does not change the file. Changes happen only when you edit a field or a permission setting in the window.

task: Read a file's details in Finder
appliesTo: macOS 27 Finder, plus iCloud Drive on iCloud.com
requirements: A Mac running macOS 27, the version these steps were checked against
The file visible in a Finder window or on the desktop
An administrator account if you need to change disk permissions

steps.name: Select the file
steps.text: Open Finder from the Dock and open the folder that holds the file. Files on the desktop work the same way. Click the file once so it is highlighted.
steps.tip: Click the name or the icon. Empty space does not select the file.

steps.name: Open Get Info from the File menu
steps.text: Click File in the menu bar at the top of the screen. Choose Get Info. The information window opens for the file you selected.

steps.name: Or press Command-I
steps.text: With the file selected and Finder active, press Command-I. The same window opens. Use the menu instead if the shortcut does not respond.
steps.tip: The shortcut only works when Finder is the active app.

steps.name: Read the details and close the window
steps.text: Check the type, size and dates. Look at the location to see which folder or iCloud Drive holds the item. Click the close button in the top-left corner when you finish. Closing the window does not change the file.

steps.name: Get summary info for several files
steps.text: Select the group of files. Hold the Control key and open the File menu. Choose Get Summary Info. Apple says a separate window opens for each item.
steps.tip: Start with a small group. Many windows at once are hard to track.

steps.name: Select the disk for permissions
steps.text: Select the disk you want to check, for example from the Finder sidebar or on the desktop. Apple's permissions steps start with the disk.

steps.name: Open Sharing & Permissions
steps.text: With the disk selected, choose File > Get Info. Click the disclosure arrow beside Sharing & Permissions to expand that section.

steps.name: Open the permission settings
steps.text: If the lock in the bottom-right corner of the panel is closed, click it. Follow the prompt macOS shows you. If you are not an administrator, ask an administrator for access instead.
steps.tip: The Ignore ownership on this volume checkbox does not appear on disks used for Time Machine backups.

steps.name: Turn on the path bar
steps.text: Open the View menu and choose Show Path Bar. The folder path appears inside the Finder window. If the path bar is hidden, hold Option to see it briefly.

steps.name: Copy a folder path
steps.text: Control-click a folder in the path bar. Choose Copy "folder" as Pathname, where the folder name fills in the placeholder. Paste the path wherever you need it.

steps.name: Show item info under icons
steps.text: Switch the Finder window to Icon view. Open View > Show View Options and select Show item info. Apple says this option works only in Icon view.

steps.name: Check an iCloud Drive file on the web
steps.text: Open icloud.com/iclouddrive in a browser and sign in. Select the file or folder. Click More in the top-right corner, then choose Get Info.
steps.tip: The web panel shows fewer fields than Finder's window.

shortcuts.action: Get Info for the selected file

troubleshooting.fix: Click the file first so it is selected, and make sure Finder is the active app. If the shortcut still fails, choose File > Get Info from the menu bar.
Select the disk, open Get Info, expand Sharing & Permissions, and click the closed lock so the settings open. If you are not an administrator, ask one to change the access for you.

troubleshooting.problem: The Ignore ownership on this volume checkbox is missing
troubleshooting.fix: The checkbox is for disks only. It does not appear for disks used for Time Machine backups, so use a different disk or ask an administrator.

troubleshooting.problem: Video Duration shows --:-- in Get Info on Tahoe
troubleshooting.fix: Open the video in QuickTime Player and press Command-I to use the Inspector. One Apple Community report describes this workaround, and Apple has not confirmed a cause or fix.

troubleshooting.problem: iCloud.com Get Info shows fewer details than Finder
troubleshooting.fix: That is expected. The web panel covers iCloud Drive files only. Open the file in Finder on your Mac for the full window.

troubleshooting.problem: The path bar will not show
troubleshooting.fix: Choose View > Show Path Bar. If it is still hidden, hold Option briefly to see the path.
